_note: The knock that forces a substitution (decision Y, ADR-066, OI-110). The force of a foul's contact is the offender's approach speed in thousandths of the reference speed (the fact Law 12 reads for the card), weighed by the fouled man's body: force x (0.5 + injury_proneness). At knock_force_milli or more he cannot go on: he leaves the pitch, and his side must replace him (Law 3) or play a man short. No die (ADR-035). Grade 2, fixed on the effect: the real substitutions before the 45th minute not after a red card of the same side, almost all of them forced, Serie A 2017-18 (Wyscout public dataset, Pappalardo et al. 2019, matches_Italy.json and events_Italy.json): 0.19 a match on the 190 matches with an even id, 0.25 on the 190 with an odd id. Fixed on the engine's 120 matches with an even seed (42-281): 0.19 knocks in the first half a match; held out on the 120 with an odd seed: 0.19, against the real 0.25 (the two real halves differ by 0.06 themselves: sampling, about 0.035 for each). Consistent with the UEFA Elite Club Injury Study (Ekstrand, Hägglund and Waldén 2011, British Journal of Sports Medicine 45:553-558: 27.5 injuries per 1000 match hours, about 0.9 a match, most from contact): not every injury forces the man off at once. How long and what kind of injury it is belongs to L1.
